hints: Focus on what increasing concentration actually changes, the crowding of particles in the same volume, not their energy.
With more $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$ particles in the same total volume, iodine and propanone particles meet each other more often.
Connect more frequent meetings per second to a faster rate, remembering that temperature, not concentration, decides what fraction has enough energy.
walkthrough:
**Picture what higher concentration means**

Think of the same beaker volume but with more propanone particles squeezed in. They are closer together, not further apart.

$$\text{higher concentration} = \text{more particles per unit volume}$$

**Apply collision theory**

For reaction, $\text{I}_2$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$ must collide with correct orientation and enough energy. More particles in the same space means more collisions per second.

$$\text{I}_2(\text{aq}) + \text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3(\text{aq}) \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{I}(\text{aq}) + \text{HI}(\text{aq})$$

**Separate frequency from energy**

Concentration does not give particles more energy and does not change the proportion that is successful. That is controlled by temperature and activation energy. It simply increases the total number of collisions per second, so more successful collisions per second occur and rate increases.

options.A: Incorrect. The proportion or fraction of successful collisions depends on energy, temperature and activation energy, not concentration. Concentration increases the total number of collisions, so the number of successful collisions per second rises, but the proportion stays about the same.
options.B: Incorrect and opposite to the truth. Higher concentration in the same volume means particles are closer together and more crowded, not further apart. This crowding is exactly why they collide more often.
options.C: Incorrect. Adding more propanone does not make individual particles move faster or have more kinetic energy. Average kinetic energy is set by temperature, which has not changed here. This is a common confusion between concentration and temperature effects.
options.D: Correct. With more propanone particles in the same total volume, $\text{I}_2$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$ collide more frequently per second. Even with the same success proportion, more collisions per second gives more successful collisions per second, so the rate increases.
